name: Gulf South Gas Pipeline / Texas Gateway Project
researcher_notes: Not an existing row. P5932 (Texas to Mississippi Expansion, operating, 243 mi from Keatchie) and P7810 (Kosciusko Junction, Mississippi) are different projects. Gulf South Pipeline Company, a Boardwalk Pipelines subsidiary, announced a binding open season on October 30, 2025 for about 155 miles of new greenfield pipe from its Carthage Header in Texas to Beauregard Parish, Louisiana, with new compression and metering, plus upgrades to its existing Index 129 line including a new compressor station near Cleveland, Texas. Minimum capacity is 1,450,000 Dth per day and a foundation shipper has signed a precedent agreement. Target in service is November 1, 2029. The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects release for August 2026 (sheet Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, Excel row 120, project Texas Gateway Project) states 155 miles, 1,450 MMcf/d, 36 and 42 inch (first 67 miles 36 inch, remaining 87 miles 42 inch), status Applied, FERC docket CP26-547, application filed June 26, 2026. An Oil & Gas Journal report from July 2026 also states the FERC filing. EIA is one release; the operator press release, a trade press article and the Oil & Gas Journal report are independent of it. Capacity is in MMcf/d as listed by EIA; the operator states 1,450,000 Dth/d. No cost stated in the sources checked. Ends at Beauregard Parish, near Gillis hub; no exact endpoint stated. Owner spelled as on the sheet for other Boardwalk rows (Boardwalk Pipeline Partners); the operating entity is Gulf South Pipeline Company LLC. Route: no official GIS or map checked, so none staged. Confidence high.
